summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only list of Chaos Engineering resources covering culture, books, tutorials, tools, papers, gamedays, blogs, conferences and forums.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is an "awesome" style markdown list of links rather than software. It is organized into sections: Culture, Books, Education, Notable Tools, Retired tools, Cloud Services, Papers, Gamedays, Blogs & Newsletters, Podcasts, Conferences & Meetups, and Forums. The Notable Tools section is the largest and gives a one-line description per tool, covering Kubernetes, Docker, AWS, Azure, Spring Boot, JVM, BOSH, Go, and frontend (React, Vue) targets. The Culture and Education sections point to talks, articles, and tutorials. The README has a short definition of chaos engineering and a Contributing pointer, and it does not include install steps.
use_cases: Finding chaos engineering tools for Kubernetes, Docker, AWS or Azure
Learning the principles and practice of chaos engineering
Planning a gameday or chaos day for a team
Finding books, papers, and talks on resilience testing
Discovering chaos engineering communities, meetups, and newsletters
Comparing alternatives to Chaos Monkey and similar fault injection tools
notable: Very broad coverage: over 100 tools listed, grouped by platform (Kubernetes, Docker, AWS, Azure, JVM, BOSH)
Includes a Gamedays section with worked examples from Gremlin, Target, New Relic and others
Separates retired tools (Simian Army, ChaoSlingr) from active ones
Includes security chaos engineering resources alongside general reliability material
caveats: It is a list of links only; the README does not verify whether linked tools or articles are still maintained
Some entries are vendor pages or SaaS offerings (for example Gremlin, steadybit, Proofdock), and some tools are marked as retired
The README gives no install or usage instructions for any tool
